lesson_title: Which Way, How Fast, How Hard
hook_text: One term, one headgear, one exam. Here is all of Term 3 Technology in sixty seconds.
clip_script: Gears: meshed pairs turn opposite ways. Ratio is driven teeth over driver teeth; 12 at 1 200 rpm driving 36 gives 3, so 400 rpm out, slower and three times stronger. An idler flips direction and leaves the ratio alone. Stages multiply: 60 over 12 twice is 25. Bevels turn corners. Mechanical advantage: load over effort, or for a lever effort arm over load arm from the fulcrum; crowbar 1.5 over 0.25 is 6, so 900 newtons needs 150. For gears, MA equals the ratio; above one is force, below one is speed. Drawings: gears as circles with tooth counts, systems as three boxes with numbers, working drawings in first angle, thick, dashed, chain. Design process: brief without the solution, measurable specifications, compared ideas, drawing, budget, safe making, evaluation with numbers. Show your working, flip at every mesh, check who drives, leave nothing blank.
visual_style: Whiteboard in three columns; gears spin with ratios; a crowbar balances with 1.5 and 0.25; three boxes fill with rpm; a headgear outline labels back-leg, legs, bracing and beam with force words.
pacing: Gears, MA, drawings and process, habits.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and work three gear-ratio questions with the driver swapped each time.
